_schema.description: 2026 Legislative Assembly results from the VEC's public results website, read every 5 minutes on election night by scripts/results.py. 'Called' is this site's projection (see call_rule), not the VEC's; a seat the VEC has declared is called by the VEC. Source: Victorian Electoral Commission.

fields.source: {name, url}: the VEC results pages this was read from
fields.profile: Which URL-map profile produced it ('2026'; '2022' only in tests)
fields.vec_updated: The latest 'last updated' time shown on any VEC page read (raw text as published)
fields.tally: {called: {bloc: seats}, leading: {bloc: seats}, undecided, counted_seats, majority}; blocs ALP, LNP, GRN, ONP, OTH
fields.districts: {district id: {name, url, vec_updated, fetched, enrolment, formal, informal, total, counted_pct (of enrolment), centres_counted, centres_total, declared, elected {name, party}, candidates [{id, name, party, party_name, votes, pct}], tcp [{id, name, party, votes, pct}] or null, tcp_basis (2cp | distribution), leader {id, name, party, basis}, margin_votes, uncounted_estimate, status (called | leading | undecided), called_by (vec | site | null), holder (party before the election), changes_hands, swing_2cp (leader's 2CP change since 2022, same pair only), declaration_votes {early_cast, postal_returned, as_of (the VEC's pre-election figures, early_votes.json), early_counted, postal_counted (formal first preferences of those types so far), outstanding} or null when the VEC published no district figures}}

call_rule.text: Called by this site when the leader's two-candidate-preferred margin is larger than the estimated uncounted vote plus a buffer (the larger of 250 votes and 1% of enrolment), so the trailing candidate couldn't catch up even with every remaining vote. Uncounted = enrolment x the seat's 2022 turnout - votes counted, or, if larger, the early and postal votes the VEC says were cast that aren't in the count yet. A seat the VEC has declared is called by the VEC.
